fun_highlights: The callback system is the game's crown jewel. When Iris Brandt (Dynasty 1, gen 2) looks away from a sleeping rough person and the card text explicitly recalls 'the lonely child in the yard, the time she looked away' — that is a genuine moral dilemma with history behind it. The choice is harder precisely because we watched her make the first cowardice. The cb_lookaway, cb_principle, cb_study_pays, and cb_books_late arcs all land this way: the decision at age 57 feels weightier than it would cold because it echoes a decision at age 10.

The competing-goods cards (x_honest_or_kind, x_loyalty_truth, x_dream_or_duty) have real teeth. Neither option is clean. 'A kindness and an honesty — and they will not both fit in the room' is one of the few framings in the whole game where I could not predict which choice would 'feel right.' Calla Okonkwo's cb_the_cost at age 70 — 'Decide it was right' vs 'Let it stay unsettled' — was the single most genuinely unsettling beat in the transcripts. These are the game at its best.

The vocation-forking at y_calling is robust. A soldier life (Ren Salvedi going where it's worst, carrying the war at 3am, refusing to talk about it) feels structurally different from a scholar life (Iris Brandt's 40-year research arc, the knowledge-give-or-guard dilemma, the 'hand the unanswered question on' elder beat). That structural divergence means choices at age 19 genuinely redirect which 5-6 later beats are even eligible — meaningful consequence, not cosmetic.

The e_bequest card is a genuine dynasty-layer choice. 'Everything I know' vs 'Every coin I can spare' vs 'The stories and the warmth' vs 'Nothing but their own freedom' each produce visibly different starting conditions. I saw Iris bequest knowledge and watched the scholarly reputation lock in; that generational weight is real. A choice made at age 75 shapes play 80 years later in a different person.

The era-coloring of choice framings adds real freshness. The a_marry card during a war era reads 'There is a war on, and they have stopped pretending the future is guaranteed. The question of marrying has gone, suddenly, from someday to now or perhaps never.' That is a materially different dilemma than the settled-era version. The y_calling card in a war era likewise gates soldier as the urgent obvious choice against the others. These aren't cosmetic — they tilt what both options mean.

The body-as-constraint elder beats (e_body's 'push on regardless' vs 'slow down') give teeth to late-life choices that have no equivalent in most life-sims. The frail-trait lives play visibly differently (Pavel Ashby's whole midlife is the negotiation), and the 'push on regardless' option setting P.flags.peril is a rare case of a soft, meditative choice having a downstream mechanical consequence.
staleness: The childhood sequence is a near-identical checklist across almost every life in the transcripts. By Dynasty 6 a reader can predict: c_origin, then one of {c_unfair, c_wonder, c_book}, then c_move or c_sibling, then c_grandparent, then c_dark or c_friend. The trait-affinity system (TRAIT_AFFINITY in engine.js) is supposed to differentiate this by routing warm children to c_friend and restless to c_move, but the pool is small enough (8-9 child cards total, all once:true) that all lives see most of them regardless. Ronja Brandt, Henrik Brandt, and Calla Okonkwo all hit c_wonder + c_unfair + c_move in consecutive dynasties with only cosmetic variation in the outcome lines.

The calling-card summary lines repeat verbatim within a session. 'Chose the maker's trade — a craft, a bench, a steady narrow door into a sufficient life' appears in Henrik Brandt (gen 3), Idris Salvedi (gen 5), and Anders Sereno (founder) within these 15 dynasties. The logLine pools for y_calling are shallow (3 variants per vocation): the engine marks the card once:true per life, but within a multi-dynasty session the same 3 lines rotate visibly. The same problem hits the late-love pool ('found love later than expected, and was almost embarrassed by the size of it' vs the two other a_meet_late variants — Dynasty 8 founder Noor and Dynasty 9 Anders Sereno both use the same arc within 3 dynasties of each other).

The 'Kept the door open' / open-table-hospitality beat appears in Iris Brandt gen 2, Edmund Ashby gen 2, Ottilie Mercer founder, Lazlo Bjornsen founder, Greta Ashby gen 3, Noor Ashby founder, and Yara Okonkwo gen 3 — 7 of 15 dynasties. The a_neighbour card and the 'keep the door open' choice of a_child's no-child variant and a separate 'keep door open' line from another card all converge on the same outcome text. The player who plays 3+ dynasties will have read some version of 'ran an open house she couldn't afford and counted the warmth of it worth every coin' in nearly half of all lives.

The war-trauma callback (cb_reckless-adjacent, the war-at-3am card) fires in Carys Brandt (soldier), Ren Salvedi (soldier), Cyrus Ashby (soldier), Linnea Okonkwo (soldier), and Theda Quint (soldier) — every soldier life in the transcripts hits it, and nearly every one pairs it with the 'carry it alone' or 'talk about it finally' binary in the same late-middle-age band. This is the most predictable beat in the game: if you chose 'the blade,' you will eventually face this card. It's well-written, but its inevitability makes it feel like a vocation tax rather than a surprise.

The 'Decide the kindest inheritance was none at all, and let the next life be wholly its own' / nothing-but-freedom bequest choice appears word-for-word in Tobias Ashby, Linnea Salvedi, and is available to almost every long-lived parent with no competing pressures. The bequest card is potentially the game's most interesting dynasty-layer choice, but the 'Nothing but their own freedom' option has a particularly beautiful outcome line that I noticed appearing frequently enough that it becomes recognizable rather than surprising.

Observation lines from the observe() function in engine.js recycle visibly within a single session. 'There is a whole life she keeps behind the eyes, and visits often' fires for Iris Brandt gen 2 AND Linnea Salvedi gen 3 — the same exact line. 'The stairs have started to ask a question of them' is the near-universal vit<35 trigger and appears in some variant in virtually every life past 50. These ambient lines are not choices, but they constitute the texture between choices, and when a reader sees 'the body has begun keeping its own quiet counsel' for the fourth time across 15 dynasties, it damages the sense of each life as singular.

improvements.what: Add 3-4 new childhood cards that gate on era rather than trait, and raise the onceDyn cooldown on existing child cards from the default 3 to 5-6 generations.
improvements.why: The childhood sequence is the first thing a returning player recognizes. Trait affinity alone doesn't differentiate enough because most traits appear in most lives. Era-gated child cards (something only a plague-era or war-era child faces) would guarantee structural divergence in early life without requiring more child cards overall. A higher onceDyn keeps the best existing beats (c_dark, c_friend) from cycling back every 3 dynasties.

improvements.what: Double the logLine variant pools for the four vocation paths in y_calling (currently 3 variants each), and give a_meet_late and the open-table beat (keep-the-door-open branch) 5-6 distinct outcome lines instead of 2-3.
improvements.why: These are the most frequently-reached nodes in the graph. The engine's freshPick deduplication works within a life but not across dynasties in a session. A reader who plays 8+ lives will see the same 3 scholar/soldier/maker/wanderer summary lines multiple times. More variants at high-traffic nodes is the highest-leverage prose investment.

improvements.what: Give the war-trauma callback (the 'war at 3am' card) a mandatory alt framing that isn't the talk/carry binary — e.g., a third option that externalizes it differently (action, ritual, distance) — and add one new midlife soldier card that has nothing to do with trauma, so soldier lives aren't 70% war-adjacent.
improvements.why: The soldier vocation currently reads as 'person who has trauma': every soldier life hits go-where-worst + war-at-3am + optional name/grave. A third trauma choice would at minimum differentiate the texture. A positive soldier card (mastery, leadership, the odd dignity of the profession) would make soldier a richer selection rather than just a route to the dark.

improvements.what: Introduce one hard-asymmetric choice per vocation that only appears if earlier choices built a specific pattern — for scholars: only if both 'chase the question' and 'guard it' were chosen across different generations; for soldiers: only if two generations both went where it was worst. These compound-condition gates make dynasty-planning feel like it has mechanical teeth.
improvements.why: Right now the dynasty layer is primarily atmospheric (reputation drifts, mottos crystallize, heirlooms accumulate) but the actual choices are per-life. A compound-condition card that requires specific multi-generational patterns would make the player feel that earlier decisions built toward something only this combination could unlock — the deepest form of choice meaningfulness.

improvements.what: Add 8-10 new observe() ambient lines to the mid-tier stat buckets (spirit 45-65, heart 45-65, means 35-65) and reduce the firing probability of low-bucket lines like 'the stairs have started to ask a question' to 0.12% rather than firing whenever the threshold is crossed.
improvements.why: The observe() ambient lines are the prose texture of the years between choices. The current pools are deep for the extreme buckets but thin for the common middle range, so most lives share the same 3-4 ambient lines in their middle decades. These aren't choices, but they're what the player reads 60% of the time. Better coverage here reduces the sense of template without requiring any new choice cards.

verdict: A Life earns its score on the strength of its callback architecture and its genuine competing-goods dilemmas — when Iris Brandt encounters the person sleeping rough at 61, knowing she looked away from that child at 10, the game is doing something most life-sims cannot. But a player who runs 4+ dynasties will encounter a recognizable template: childhood checklist, calling fork, open-table hospitality beat, war-trauma-if-soldier, and a late-life reckoning — all with finite text pools that start cycling visibly by the second hour. The choice-savorer's core complaint is that the best dilemmas (x_dream_or_duty, cb_the_cost, x_honest_or_kind) are outnumbered by high-frequency nodes where the choices are real but the outcome prose has already been read. The fix is mostly prose depth and variant expansion at the traffic bottlenecks, not structural surgery — the engine and dynasty layers are well-designed and the generational weight is genuine.
